                    ### Question
                    A 22-year-old patient consulted for a decrease in painful visual acuity in the left eye. It is diagnosed of optic neuritis. Indicate which of the following findings would allow a diagnosis of definitive multiple sclerosis in this patient:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Oligoclonal bands in cerebrospinal fluid.
opb. Alteration of visual evoked potentials (increase in P100 wave latency in both eyes).
opc. Second attack 3 months later with involvement of the cerebellum.
opd. Initial MRI with multiple (> 8) bilateral periventricular lesions in T2 sequences.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
To definitively diagnose multiple sclerosis in a patient with optic neuritis, the finding of a second attack 3 months later with involvement of the cerebellum would fulfill the dissemination in time and space criteria for multiple sclerosis. This finding is the most indicative of definitive multiple sclerosis in this case.
